purpose: AUTOHAWK resale-value database for Germany. Built from user feedback, local scan logs, sold/reserved examples and conservative flipper logic. It is a decision aid, not a mechanical guarantee.

strategy.main_customer: young buyer / first car / quick clean resale, with separate scoring for flip-profit vs buyer-value
strategy.core_rule: Do not search for normal market cars. A candidate must be clearly below the lower observed market band, or have a motivated seller signal that creates negotiation room, while staying technically safe.
strategy.best_available_rule: If no HOT exists, show only the best 5-10 CHECK candidates, not every surviving listing.
strategy.hard_lesson: Retail/normal price is not opportunity. Good listings must either be under the lower market band, have urgent/motivated seller wording, or be unusually clean with long HU/TUV and low risk.
price_truth_rules: Use lower market band/q1/30th percentile for old liquid flip cars, not median asking price.
Market +/-7 percent is not enough edge for flipping.
7-12 percent below market is only interesting with urgent seller, strong proof, or exceptional condition.
12-20 percent below lower market band is the normal minimum for interesting flip candidates.
20-30 percent below lower market band is strong but requires a cheap reason, not engine/gearbox/rust/document risk.
Umzug, muss weg, dringend, neues Auto gekauft, Platzmangel, keine Zeit and VB are motivated-seller signals; they boost priority but do not remove the need for discount/proof.
strategy.segment_rule: Never mix personal buyer value with flip profit. A Focus can be a strong buyer-value lead while still only CHECK for flip unless price is below lower market band.
strategy.model_trust_rule: Fresh TUV, low km and petrol are strong positives, but model mismatch (for example Micra/Qashqai conflict) makes market price and risk analysis unreliable. Such listings stay CHECK until exact model is confirmed by seller/Fahrzeugschein/FIN.
strategy.high_mileage_workhorse_rule: High mileage is not an automatic reject when the car is a cheap practical workhorse: simple NA petrol, timing belt done, Kombi/body practicality, tow hitch, private seller, and low entry price. Keep CHECK, not HOT, if Euro4, age 18+ or TUV under 12 months.

strong_boosts: cheap entry price from private seller
strong_penalties: TUV under 12 months on old car

observed_feedback_examples.lesson: Sold/reserved quickly. Simple Polo with long TUV, Klima and normal condition is a real demand signal.
Repeated Polo demand. Clean cheap Polo should be prioritized, but no TUV/rust/DSG/TSI must be punished.
Reserved quickly. Yaris is low-risk and liquid if TUV/service/rust are okay.
Reserved quickly despite small issues. Cheap Focus can work, but engine cold start, rust and TUV decide.

Deleted/sold very quickly after scan. Cheap simple Swift around 1500-1900 EUR has stronger real demand than the raw score suggested. Buyers prefer simple Japanese petrol, low running costs and less fear than old Golf/Polo with rust/TSI/DSG/overpriced ads.

User feedback: Focus can be more attractive than microcars for a young driver because it feels like a real car and has enough power/stability for Autobahn. If condition is clean, TUV is valid and engine is simple, Focus deserves higher personal-buyer priority even when pure flip margin is not huge.

Fresh TUV + 120k km + petrol + Japanese small car + service done is attractive, but Micra/Qashqai inconsistency, 3 doors and template description reduce trust. App must not treat this as HOT; require exact model confirmation and documents before using market price.

A 214k km car can still be useful if it is a cheap practical Kombi with 1.6 naturally aspirated petrol, timing belt replaced, tow hitch and private seller. But Euro4, 18+ years old and TUV under 12 months keep it as CHECK only; profit depends on rust, cold start, clutch, suspension and invoices.

cards.notes: One of the best youth/first-car flip models. Not necessarily cheap, but very easy to explain and resell if clean.

Repeated real feedback: Polo sells fast. Old 9N/9N3 with HU/TUV under 1700 EUR can be a priority lead. 2500-3000 EUR is only good with proof such as chain/service/TUV/clean body; otherwise margin is tight.

Golf demand is huge, but price discipline matters. Golf 5 above 3000 EUR is usually retail unless it has long TUV, clean body, simple engine, 5 doors and strong service proof. FSI/TSI/DSG should not become HOT without proof.

Segmented logic: i10 is strong safe-first-car/low-cost stock, especially low km with TUV. It can sell well to practical buyers, but it is less emotional and less Autobahn-capable than Focus. Flip only if bought below lower market band.
Very useful budget car. Good price/quality, but do not overpay just because it is clean.
Fiesta is good beginner liquidity with simple 1.25/1.3/1.4 petrol and HU/TUV. At 1200-1800 EUR it is best-available; above 3000 EUR it needs exceptional proof and is usually not quick flip.

Segmented logic: Focus Mk2 can be a strong buyer-value lead for young drivers because it feels like a real car and is Autobahn-capable. It is NOT automatically a flip-profit lead. Promote it only when price is clearly below the lower observed market band, condition is clean, HU/TUV is valid, and drivetrain is simple petrol/manual. Otherwise keep as CHECK.
Low-risk and trusted. Strong for normal buyers; margin depends on buying below the usual Toyota premium.
Aygo is safe first-car material. Long TUV at 1500-2000 EUR is attractive for buyer service; HOT only if clearly below observed market or very clean.

Segmented logic: Fabia is practical and liquid when clean. Dented bumper, heavy scratches or tired body reduce buyer emotion and resale speed unless the price is clearly below lower market band. Do not let cheap practicality outrank clean buyer-value cars automatically.
Good practical value, but old Astra can be overestimated. Must be priced right.
Good if cheap and clean, weaker than Polo/Fabia but still sellable.
Trusted, practical, low-risk. Buyers like it, but it is less emotional than VW.

Mazda 2 is reliable and good for safe buyer service, but resale is slower than Polo/Yaris/Corsa. Fresh TUV + 1.Hand around 1800-2300 EUR is good; quick flip needs either low buy price or unusually clean body.

Field update 2026-05-21: cheap Swift 1.3 Comfort around 1700 EUR was deleted/sold quickly. Treat simple petrol Swift as stronger fast-sale stock than before. It attracts first-car buyers who want reliable, cheap, small Japanese cars and are tired of overpriced/rusty Golf/Polo. Best pocket: 1300-1900 EUR with HU/TUV; check rust, clutch, warning lights and accident/tuning signs.
Budget city car. Works when cheap and clean.

A3 8P is attractive for young buyers and can sell fast if cheap, simple and clean. Best pocket: 1.6 MPI/manual with HU/TUV, Klima and 8-fach around 2000-2500 EUR. Check rust on arches/sills/door bottoms/front fenders, OBD, warning lights, oil/coolant leaks and clutch. FSI/TFSI/DSG/no-TUV must stay strict.
Can be attractive for youth, but no TUV or weak description is immediate reject.
Emotional demand exists, but strict: no TUV/rust/engine issue means reject.
Very good first-car profile; less hype than VW, but reliable and easy to sell when clean.
Practical and trusted enough. Good family/daily car, but not as fast as Polo/up/Yaris.
Strong practical demand, especially Combi. Mileage can be higher if history is real.
Youth appeal is strong, but sporty trims can be abused. Clean boring Leon is safer.
Reliable and respected, but audience is narrower. Good condition matters more than low price.
Reliable but rust is the key. Clean body can be a strong buy.
Can be cheap and okay, but weaker trust than Toyota/VW. Needs clean TUV and simple engine.
Good budget beginner car. Less emotional, but cheap clean examples sell.
Practical but not stylish. Works for families/budget buyers if cheap and clean.
Underrated cheap reliable car. Good for low budget, but buyer pool smaller than VW.
Simple, low-cost city car. Not exciting, but sensible buyers like it.
Cheap rational buy. Good for budget clients, less image but easy to justify.
Same logic as Aygo/C1: cheap, simple, small margins.

C1/Aygo/107 is strong low-budget beginner stock. At 1000-1400 EUR with HU/TUV it deserves priority manual check even with ugly photos. Margins are small; clutch, rust, exhaust, brakes and crash signs decide.
Strong style demand, especially young buyers, but condition/electrics matter and 3-door limits practicality.
Not a target youth-flip model. Practical but slower and riskier than Fiesta/Focus. Diesel + PowerShift should be rejected unless extremely cheap with proof; it can destroy all margin.

manual_review_2026_05_20.source: User + AUTOHAWK log review after 20 scans. These are field-learning examples, not guaranteed condition reports.
manual_review_2026_05_20.core_lesson: Best candidates are not the cleanest ads. They are liquid cars in the correct buy-zone with HU/TUV and no expensive drivetrain/body/document red flags.
ranking_logic: First decide who buys the car after us.
Then check whether the buy price leaves room after preparation, repair reserve and resale negotiation.
Then punish expensive hidden risks: gearbox, engine, structural rust, no TUV, accident, warning lights.
Ugly photos, dirty interior or weak ad text can be opportunity only when the model is liquid and the technical risk is controllable.

reviewed_candidates.why: A3 badge is liquid for young buyers, 1.6 manual is the safer simple drivetrain, Klima + 8-fach + TUV are resale signals. Around 2100 EUR can be a real buy-zone if the body and dashboard are clean.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Rust on arches/sills/door bottoms/front fenders, accident panel gaps, OBD, ABS/airbag/check-engine lights, clutch, oil leaks, cooling temperature/thermostat, windows/locks.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Do not treat all old Audis as bad. A3 1.6 manual with TUV under 2500 EUR is a priority CHECK; FSI/TFSI/DSG/no-TUV remains strict reject or low CHECK.

reviewed_candidates.why: C1/Aygo/107 platform is cheap, simple and good first-car material. 1000 EUR with TUV is interesting even at higher mileage because the buyer pool exists.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Clutch bite/slip, rust underneath, exhaust, brakes, crash history, warning lights, interior wear vs mileage.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: C1 around 1000-1400 EUR with TUV should be elevated to best-available even if photos are ugly. Margins are small but risk is usually controllable.

reviewed_candidates.why: TUV neu + 1.Hand is a strong trust signal. Mazda 2 is reliable and easy to recommend, but resale speed is weaker than Polo/Yaris/Corsa.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Rear arches, sills, underbody rust, clutch, brakes, service history, dashboard warnings.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Mazda 2 at 1800-2300 EUR with fresh TUV and 1.Hand is good for safe buyer service; for quick flip it needs either low buy price or unusually clean condition.

reviewed_candidates.why: Polo with TUV under 1500 EUR is exactly the market pocket that can move fast. Even average condition can sell if technical state is honest.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Rust, chain noise on cold start for 1.2, clutch, oil leaks, ABS/airbag/check-engine, exact TUV report.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Old Polo 9N/9N3 under 1700 EUR with TUV should outrank many cleaner but retail-priced cars.

reviewed_candidates.why: Simple petrol Fiesta is a normal beginner car. Good liquidity, cheap repair, but at high mileage it needs TUV and no serious rust.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Rust around sills/rear arches, clutch, coolant, brakes, TUV, dashboard warnings.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Fiesta 1.25/1.3/1.4 petrol at 1200-1800 EUR with TUV can be a good best-available lead, but not HOT at market price.

reviewed_candidates.why: TUV + Steuerkette neu is strong proof. Price is already closer to retail, so it is better for safe buyer service than quick flip.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Invoice for chain, TUV report, rust, clutch, OBD, private vs dealer.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Polo at 2500-3000 EUR needs strong proof and condition to remain interesting; margin must be capped.

reviewed_candidates.why: Aygo with long TUV is low-risk first-car stock. It is not always huge profit, but it is easy to explain and resell.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Clutch, water pump/coolant, rust underneath, exhaust, accident signs.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Aygo/C1/107 with long TUV in 1500-2000 EUR range is safe buyer-service material; HOT only if clearly under market.

reviewed_candidates.why: Diesel + PowerShift is not good youth-flip risk. Gearbox/DPF/EGR/turbo risk can destroy all margin.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Only consider with massive discount and gearbox proof, otherwise skip.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: PowerShift should be a hard market-fear penalty and should not appear as a strong CHECK.

reviewed_candidates.why: Golf is liquid, but this price is not a flip price unless it is very clean, long TUV, 5-door, service proof and no rust.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Rust, engine variant, TUV, dashboard lights, clutch/gearbox, accident.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Golf 5 above 3000 EUR must be capped unless proof and market discount are unusually strong.

reviewed_candidates.why: Cheap Corsa can work if TUV and body are okay. It is less exciting than Polo/Yaris but still liquid.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Rust, chain noise for small petrol, oil leaks, coolant, TUV, clutch.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Corsa around 1200-1800 EUR with TUV is a valid best-available car; over 3000 EUR needs strong proof.

reviewed_candidates.why: Astra J with long TUV can be a decent normal purchase, but 3500 EUR is not automatically a flip.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Rust/brakes, clutch, oil leaks, coolant, service, seller type.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Astra J at 3000-3800 EUR should be buyer-service CHECK, not HOT, unless market evidence shows real discount.

reviewed_candidates.why: Practical and cheap with TUV, but less liquid than Polo/Corsa/Yaris. Good only if condition is honest.
reviewed_candidates.must_check: Clutch, electronics, rust, brakes, TUV report, warning lights.
reviewed_candidates.database_lesson: Cheap practical French cars can be best-available but should not outrank stronger German/Japanese city cars unless price is very low.
